output.model_sql:
with tmp_first as (
    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_ts)::date as first_order_date
    from {{ source('raw', 'orders') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id
)

select
    c.customer_id,
    c.region,
    c.segment,
    c.signup_date,
    c.marketing_opt_in,
    f.first_order_date
from {{ source('raw', 'customers') }} c
left join tmp_first f
    on f.customer_id = c.customer_id
output.notes: The temp table tmp_first becomes a CTE. The model reads raw.orders directly, not stg_orders_clean, so it sees exactly the rows the legacy job sees. Swapping in the cleaned staging model could change first_order_date. The job has no post-CREATE UPDATE, DELETE or INSERT statements to fold in. Column order matches the legacy table. Nothing in the job depends on run time or randomness.
quirks_found: first_order_date is the minimum over all raw orders regardless of status. Cancelled, failed or test orders still count toward a customer's first order date.
raw.orders is used as-is (not deduplicated or cleaned). Duplicate loads don't change the MIN, but bad or late-loaded rows with an early order_ts would.
The timestamp is cast to DATE after taking the MIN. The date reflects whatever timezone or offset order_ts is stored in; no timezone conversion is applied.
Customers with no orders, or whose orders all have NULL order_ts, get NULL first_order_date because of the LEFT JOIN.
Orders whose customer_id has no match in raw.customers are silently dropped.
raw.customers is not deduplicated. Duplicate customer_id rows in the source appear as duplicate rows in the output, each with the same first_order_date.
Customer rows with a NULL customer_id are kept, with NULL first_order_date, because the LEFT JOIN on NULL never matches.
